title: Execution of the halving loop
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ be a function assigning a Boolean value to each of four indices and each finite Boolean word, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, let $b$ be a Boolean value, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a state of the eighteen registers with every register value at most $B$. There is a finite run of the program $A_E$, starting with control label $\mathrm{hv}(b,0)$, register values $\mathrm{st}$, and no answer, and ending with control label $\mathrm{cp}(\mathrm{popT}(b),0)$, counter register $C=0$, temporary register $T=\lfloor \mathrm{st}.T/2^{\mathrm{st}.C}\rfloor$, all other register values unchanged, and no answer. Every configuration strictly before the final configuration satisfies the guard: its instruction is permitted by the precondition for input $x$, and every register value is at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle assigning a Boolean to each of four indices and finite Boolean words
Every register value in $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four
indices and each finite bit string, let $x$ be a finite bit string, and let $b$ be
either Boolean value. From any state of the eighteen registers whose values are all at
most $B$, the program has a finite run starting at the halving-loop control state with
phase $0$, register values given by that state, and no answer, and ending at the
copy-loop control state for the pop routine with phase $0$, with the counter register
equal to $0$, the temporary register equal to its initial value divided by $2$ raised to
the initial counter value, every other register unchanged, and no answer. Every
configuration strictly before the final configuration satisfies the guard: its
instruction is in the permitted precondition for input $x$, and all register values are
at most $B$.
